3. Justify the use of a contrast agent such as a Barium meal when performing X ray examinations.
Barium meals are often used to image the intestines. The absorption of X rays by neighbouring tissues in this
region is too similar to generate contrast. Hence a contrast agent is introduced to ensure that different
tissues are absorbing X rays in very different amounts and thus creates contrast and a clear outline of the
organ of interest.
